rows.title: Ask 'What are you importing?' before a notification is created
rows.detail: Starting a new notification from the all-types dashboard in the INS front door asks the Design Release 2.1 notification type question first, before any draft exists. Live animals carries on to the animals frontend's existing live-animals start, which creates the GBN-AG draft and lands on origin. Germinal products, offered second under the 9 October ruling, carries on to the start of the germinal products set, the live-animals set's sibling in the animals frontend mounted at /germinal-products; the ruling lets this link land before the set itself is built. Plants for planting, Potatoes (seed and ware) and Wood products carry on to the start of the high-risk plants journey in trade-imports-plants-frontend. Abandoning the question leaves no empty draft behind.
acceptanceCriteria: Starting a new notification from the all-types dashboard shows the question 'What are you importing?' instead of going straight to an origin page, and no draft notification is created at that point: the dashboard's notification list gains no new entry while the question is open or after the user leaves it with Back (prototype:dr2-1-source app/routes.js:11112-11114; trace:prototype-dr2-1 T1; trace:e2e T01 call@286; conflicts:c-007)

The notification type page has the browser title 'What are you importing? - Import notification service - GOV.UK' and the heading 'What are you importing?' as the radios' fieldset legend (h1), with the caption 'About the consignment' inside the heading (prototype:dr2-1-source app/views/design-release-2.1/notification-type.html:7,39; trace:prototype-dr2-1 T1 action 16)

The question offers radios in this order, with no hint text on the group or any option and none pre-selected: Live animals; Germinal products (semen, ova, embryos); Plants for planting; Potatoes (seed and ware); Wood products (prototype:dr2-1-source app/routes.js:125-131; trace:prototype-dr2-1 T1 action 16; ruling:sam-2026-10-09 claim 10; conflicts:c-007)

Choosing Live animals and pressing Continue creates a new live-animals draft and lands on its 'Origin of the import' page, which shows the Draft tag and a new GBN-AG reference (prototype:dr2-1-specs e2e/about-the-consignment.fit.spec.js:65; trace:prototype-dr2-1 T1 action 44; conflicts:c-007)

Choosing Germinal products (semen, ova, embryos) and pressing Continue sends the user from the INS front door to the germinal products set's start under /germinal-products in the animals frontend, and no live-animals notification is created: the dashboard's notification list gains no live-animals entry (ruling:sam-2026-10-09 claims 1, 10 and 11; conflicts:c-007)

Choosing Plants for planting, Potatoes (seed and ware) or Wood products and pressing Continue lands on the start of the high-risk plants journey in the plants service, and no live-animals notification is created (conflicts:c-007)

Pressing Continue with nothing chosen re-shows the page with an error summary titled 'There is a problem' listing 'Select what you are importing', linked to the first radio, the same message shown inline on the radio group, and the browser title prefixed 'Error: ' (prototype:dr2-1-source app/routes.js:151-160; trace:prototype-dr2-1 T1 action 30; prototype:dr2-1-specs e2e/about-the-consignment.fit.spec.js:53-57; conflicts:c-006)

The page ends with a single 'Continue' button: there is no 'Save and return to overview' button and no cancel link (prototype:dr2-1-source app/views/design-release-2.1/notification-type.html:48-53; trace:prototype-dr2-1 T1 action 16)
The page's Back link goes to the all-types dashboard, and the service navigation highlights Dashboard (prototype:dr2-1-source app/routes.js:10606-10608; trace:prototype-dr2-1 T1 action 15)

The page shows no Draft strip and no notification reference; the origin page reached after choosing Live animals shows both (prototype:dr2-1-source app/views/design-release-2.1/notification-type.html:23-57; trace:prototype-dr2-1 T1 action 16 against action 44; conflicts:c-007)

With Welsh chosen, every string on the notification type page (title, caption, heading, the five options, the error message and the Continue button) shows its Welsh counterpart (repo:frontend features/origin/copy/copy.cy.js:1-3)
rows.gate: Look at the cross-service start before anything builds on it: the type page in the INS front door, how Live animals hands over to the animals frontend's start (today a form post with its own request forgery token), how Germinal products hands over to the germinal set's start under /germinal-products before that set exists, and how the plants types hand over to the plants service. The re-selection row, template creation's type question, the INS germinal list's Create new and the dashboard's 'Create new' button all copy this pattern.
notes: Rewrites inc-148 to the 9 October ruling: Germinal products is now the second option (ruling claim 10 sets aside the old criterion 3 that left it off) and continues to the germinal products set's start, which the ruling (claim 11) lets land before the germinal theme builds the set. The criterion observes the handover to /germinal-products, never the germinal origin page, so it holds before the set exists; the germinal set's own create row proves the landing.

req-013 (the live-animals origin Back link) moves out of this row into the re-selection row (inc-150): its template-review branch can only be observed once template editing exists, and keeping it here would hold the whole start behind the templates rows. The ruling (claim 13) split req-013 into a live half (req-013) and a germinal half (req-1740, germinal theme).

Merge order frontend, insfrontend, tests: the animals frontend's start entry must accept a start from the INS page before the INS page sends users to it. Per conflicts:c-006 the page keeps the 'Error: ' title prefix in its error state. The all-types dashboard's 'Create new' button itself (c-147) is the dashboard-home area's change; this row repoints whatever start control the dashboard has at the time to the type question. The Welsh criterion carries req-057's duty for the strings this row adds; req-057 itself sits in the origin row that finishes the page.

rows.title: Origin's Back link follows where the notification started, and the type question picks the notification back up
rows.detail: The live-animals origin page's Back link follows where the user came from: the type question for a notification started from it, the live animals notifications list for one started there, the overview when opened from the overview, and the template review while a live-animals template is being edited. Going back to the type question shows the notification's own type already chosen. Keeping that type returns to the same notification with no new draft. Choosing a different type starts a new notification of that type in its own set or service, and nothing is changed or cleared on the notification left behind (9 October ruling, c-219).
acceptanceCriteria: On a live-animals notification started from the type question, the origin page's Back link goes to the 'What are you importing?' question, which shows Live animals already selected (prototype:dr2-1-source app/routes.js:10586-10600, 10609; trace:prototype-dr2-1 T3 action 10; conflicts:c-011, c-219)

On a live-animals notification started from the live animals notifications list's own create button, the origin page's Back link goes to that list (prototype:dr2-1-source app/routes.js:10586-10600; prototype:dr2-1-specs e2e/about-the-consignment.fit.spec.js:105; conflicts:c-011)
Opened from the notification overview, the origin page's Back link goes to the overview (prototype:dr2-1-source app/routes.js:488-498; trace:prototype-dr2-1 T6 action 20; conflicts:c-011)

Opened from the template review while a saved live-animals template is being edited, the origin page's Back link goes to that template's review (prototype:dr2-1-source app/routes.js:10636, 488-498; conflicts:c-011)

Pressing Continue on the type question with Live animals still chosen returns to that same notification's origin page with the same reference, and the dashboard's notification list gains no new entry (prototype:dr2-1-source app/routes.js:11163-11168; conflicts:c-219)

Choosing Plants for planting instead and pressing Continue lands on the start of the high-risk plants journey; the live-animals notification, reopened from the dashboard, still has the same reference, Draft status and every answer it had, commodities and species included (ruling:sam-2026-10-09 claim 12; conflicts:c-007, c-219)

Choosing Germinal products (semen, ova, embryos) instead and pressing Continue sends the user to the germinal products set's start under /germinal-products, and the live-animals notification left behind keeps every answer it had (ruling:sam-2026-10-09 claims 11 and 12; conflicts:c-219)
Starting afresh from the all-types dashboard still shows the type question with nothing pre-selected (prototype:dr2-1-source app/routes.js:10609; conflicts:c-007)
notes: Rewrites inc-150 to the 9 October ruling (c-219): changing type no longer clears the live-animals notification's commodities and species; it starts the new type's own notification and leaves the old one untouched. The old criteria that cleared commodities are withdrawn with the overruled claims prototype-dr2-1-source-p2-022 and -p2-015.

Combines req-013 (the origin Back link, live half only per ruling claim 13; the germinal half is req-1740 in the germinal theme) with req-008: returning to the type question can only be observed through the origin Back link, and both are reviewed on the same two pages. Depends on inc-148 (the type question) and on inc-171, the row that makes Back links follow a template review (req-1616), so the template-edit branch of req-013 is observable when this lands. That pushes this row after the templates rows; the start itself (inc-148) is not held up.

The type pre-selected is the notification's stored category, absent meaning live animals (ruling claim 6), so a live-animals notification needs no backend change. The same mechanism serves the germinal set's origin Back link (req-1740), whose row proves Germinal products pre-selected once the set exists; that half is not written here because the germinal set lands in the last wave. Merge order frontend, insfrontend, tests: the origin Back link must carry the notification to the INS page before the INS page relies on it.

rows.title: Template creation's type question offers live animals and germinal products and leads to the template name
rows.detail: When the user is creating a template, the notification type question's Back link goes to the templates list and the service navigation highlights Templates. Choosing a type stores it on the template as a draft and goes on to the template name page instead of an origin page. Template mode offers only the types whose service stores templates, Live animals and Germinal products (9 October ruling, c-220).
acceptanceCriteria: Starting a new template shows the 'What are you importing?' question with only two radios, in this order and none pre-selected: Live animals; Germinal products (semen, ova, embryos). Plants for planting, Potatoes (seed and ware) and Wood products are not offered (ruling:sam-2026-10-09 claim 24; conflicts:c-220)
In template creation the type question's Back link goes to the templates list, and the service navigation highlights Templates (prototype:dr2-1-source app/routes.js:10606-10608; conflicts:c-007)

Choosing Live animals or Germinal products and pressing Continue goes to the template name page, not an origin page, and no draft notification is created: the dashboard's notification list gains no new entry (prototype:dr2-1-source app/routes.js:11157-11161; conflicts:c-220)
Going back from the template name page to the type question shows the type chosen for that template already selected (prototype:dr2-1-source app/routes.js:11157-11161)
notes: req-010 already sits in inc-154 ('Start a template: notification type, template name and origin in template mode'), which also holds the templates area's req-1313, req-1314 and req-1316 to req-1325. Drafted here as this area's part of that row; the combiner merges it back into inc-154 and keeps that id. The criteria overlap req-1314 (only Live animals and Germinal products, Back to Manage templates) on purpose: both say the same thing, and the combiner keeps one wording.

Rewritten to the 9 October ruling: template mode offers only Live animals and Germinal products (c-220); the prototype's full option list in template mode is not followed. Templates carry their type (ruling claim 10), so the template store keeps the chosen type; the germinal template's own pages come with the germinal theme.

Repos in merge order: backend (the template store holds the type), frontend (the template name page), insfrontend (the type page's template mode), tests. No templates code exists in either repo yet: the shared paths named here are where the templates rows (inc-151 onwards) will put it, and the combiner should take inc-151's touches as authoritative.

rows.title: Country of origin becomes a search box
rows.detail: The country of origin control takes Design Release 2.1's copy and behaviour: no hint, a 'Search for a country' placeholder, a search icon instead of a drop-down arrow, results that appear only once the user types, matching anywhere in the name with the match in bold, and screen-reader announcements for the results and the choice. Within the accessibility duty (conflicts:c-006) it stays a labelled 'Country of origin' accessible type-ahead over a native select that still works without JavaScript.
acceptanceCriteria: The 'Country of origin' question shows no hint text, with or without JavaScript (prototype:dr2-1-source app/views/design-release-2.1/origin-of-the-import.html:49-103; conflicts:c-009)

With JavaScript, the empty country box shows the placeholder 'Search for a country'; without JavaScript the native select still begins with the blank 'Select a country' option (prototype:dr2-1-source app/views/design-release-2.1/origin-of-the-import.html:57-102; trace:prototype-dr2-1 T6 action 18; conflicts:c-009)
Focusing or clicking the empty country box opens no list; results appear only once the user types (trace:prototype-dr2-1 T7; conflicts:c-009)

The country box shows a search icon button at its right, with the visually hidden text 'Search', and no drop-down arrow (prototype:dr2-1-source app/views/design-release-2.1/origin-of-the-import.html:57-102; conflicts:c-009)

Typing lists every place whose name contains the typed letters anywhere, ignoring case (typing 'ance' lists France; typing 'NETH' lists Netherlands), with the matching letters shown in bold in each result (trace:prototype-dr2-1 T7 actions 15-19, T2 action 17; prototype:dr2-1-specs e2e/about-the-consignment.fit.spec.js:151-154; conflicts:c-009)

The results are labelled 'Country search results' for screen readers, a polite live region announces how many results are available, and choosing one announces 'Selected <country>', for example 'Selected France' (trace:prototype-dr2-1 T7 action 19; prototype:dr2-1-source app/views/design-release-2.1/origin-of-the-import.html:101; conflicts:c-009)

The control is still labelled 'Country of origin', choosing a country still saves it and shows it back when the page is reopened, and without JavaScript the native select still saves the chosen country (conflicts:c-006; repo:frontend origin.fit.spec.js 'native select submits and persists the country code')
With Welsh chosen, the placeholder, the 'Search' button text, the results label and the announcements show their Welsh counterparts (repo:frontend features/origin/copy/copy.cy.js:1-3)

sources.ref: T6 action 18; T7 actions 15-24; T2 actions 15-18

notes: Unchanged from inc-009: its requirements and conflicts did not move in this re-distil. Combines the six country-control changes (hint, placeholder, no open-on-focus, search icon, contains-matching with bold, announcements): one control, one page, one review.

The type-ahead component is shared with port of entry and transit countries (arrival-and-transit area, which c-006 also sends to Design Release 2.1's behaviour with JavaScript), so the component change is listed as shared: the combiner puts it in the foundation theme if those rows want the same behaviour, otherwise this row scopes it to the country of origin instance. The page changes visually, so this row's ladder refreshes the origin page's visual baseline too; req-058 (the final baseline) sits in the region code row that finishes the page. The germinal products set copies the origin page after this row lands (ruling claim 2).

rows.title: Country of origin list labels subdivisions with their parent country
rows.detail: Places in the country of origin list that are subdivisions of a country show as '<territory> (<parent>)', for example 'Canary Islands (Spain)', and the list is sorted by the label shown. Which places appear, their names and the stored code stay what MDM serves through the reference data service. This follows the open question's default (c-221), which matches what the 9 October ruling does for the destination select and transit country search.
acceptanceCriteria: In the country of origin list, every place MDM serves as a subdivision of a country shows as '<subdivision name> (<parent country name>)', for example 'Canary Islands (Spain)', with or without JavaScript, and typing 'spain' in the search box lists Canary Islands (Spain) as well as Spain (trace:prototype-dr2-1 T2 action 17; trace:e2e T01 call@298; conflicts:c-221)
The country of origin list is sorted alphabetically by the label shown, so 'Canary Islands (Spain)' sits among the C entries (trace:prototype-dr2-1 T2 action 17; conflicts:c-221)

Choosing a subdivision still saves its code (ES-CN for the Canary Islands), and reopening the origin page shows 'Canary Islands (Spain)' in the box with the region code prefix ES (repo:frontend features/origin/validate.js:22-24, 148-152; conflicts:c-002, c-221)
The list holds the same places as the reference data service serves for the GBNAG_SPS_EX block, no more and no fewer (repo:referencedata GET /countries; conflicts:c-001)
openQuestions: c-221: Should the country of origin list label its subdivisions '<territory> (<parent>)', as the 9 October ruling does for the destination select and transit country search, or keep MDM's plain subdivision names? Default, which this row builds: label them '<territory> (<parent>)' and sort by the shown label, on the origin page of both sets; which places appear and their names stay what MDM serves, and the stored value stays the code.
notes: New row for req-030, which this re-distil raised as a question (c-221) with a default. Kept apart from the country search box row because it carries an open question the others do not, so a different answer changes only this row. Labels are presentation built in the frontend from the parent and subdivision names reference data already serves; the list's content stays MDM's (c-001, ruling 9 October), so no reference-data or stub change. Observable on every stack: the local stub and CDP dev serve nine subdivisions, and CDP test's real MDM serves its own. The germinal products set's origin page copies this behaviour when it copies the page.

The destination select and transit country search labels (ruling p1-136, p1-139) are other areas' rows; if the combiner finds they share the same label builder, that builder belongs in the foundation theme.

rows.title: Region of origin code, internal reference hint and the finished origin page
rows.detail: The region of origin code question takes Design Release 2.1's hint, caps the box at 5 characters in the browser, and with JavaScript writes the country prefix live as the user picks a country, showing an empty prefix slot until then; without JavaScript the server-side prefix stays as DR1 shipped it. Answering No clears a saved code. The origin task is complete only when the country and the region question are answered and, under Yes, a code is held. The internal reference hint drops its 58-character sentence (the server still enforces the limit). Every new or changed string on the origin page has Welsh, and the origin page's stored visual baseline is updated to the finished page.
acceptanceCriteria: The region of origin code question's hint reads 'Check the health certificate for a region of origin code. You can add the code later if you do not have the certificate now.' (prototype:dr2-1-source app/views/design-release-2.1/origin-of-the-import.html:133-135; trace:prototype-dr2-1 T1 action 44; conflicts:c-010)

The region code box stops typing at 5 characters and has autocomplete and spellcheck turned off; a longer code still gets the server's existing error (prototype:dr2-1-source app/views/partials/region-of-origin-code-input.html:19-29; trace:prototype-dr2-1 T1 action 44; conflicts:c-010)

With JavaScript, picking France in the country box makes the region code prefix 'FR', and then picking Netherlands makes it 'NL', with no form submission (trace:prototype-dr2-1 T5 actions 40-53, T7 action 24; conflicts:c-008)
Before any country is chosen, the revealed region code box shows an empty prefix in front of it, which fills in once a country is picked (trace:prototype-dr2-1 T1 action 44; conflicts:c-008)
Without JavaScript, the prefix still shows the saved or submitted country's code once the page is re-shown, as today (conflicts:c-008; trace:animals-fit origin-f-348e9 call@3019)

Changing a saved Yes answer with code FR-75 to No and saving clears the code: the review page shows 'Not applicable' for the region of origin code, and choosing Yes again shows an empty code box (prototype:dr2-1-source app/routes.js:11196-11201; trace:prototype-dr2-1 TRACE H action 165; conflicts:c-010)

The overview's 'Where is this consignment coming from?' task reads 'Complete' only when a country is chosen and the region of origin code question is answered: a country saved with the region question unanswered does not read 'Complete', a country with No reads 'Complete', and a country with Yes and a code reads 'Complete' (prototype:dr2-1-source app/routes.js:402-415; trace:animals-fit origin-c-706f0, origin-f-750ee call@3749)

The internal reference hint reads 'Enter any internal reference you want to use to identify this consignment, or leave blank.', with no 'It can be up to 58 characters.' sentence; a reference over 58 characters still gets the server's error naming the limit (prototype:dr2-1-source app/views/design-release-2.1/origin-of-the-import.html:155-169; trace:prototype-dr2-1 T1 action 44; conflicts:c-011)

With Welsh chosen, every new or changed string on the origin page (the country placeholder and search texts, the region hint and the internal reference hint) shows its Welsh counterpart, and no removed hint (the country hint, the 58-character sentence) is left in the Welsh copy (repo:frontend features/origin/copy/copy.cy.js:1-3)

The end-to-end suite's full-page visual baseline of the origin page shows the changed page (no country hint, the search box with its placeholder and icon, the new region hint and the shorter internal reference hint), and the visual check passes against it (trace:e2e T16 expect@50, screencast page@da77b720)

sources.ref: T1 action 44; T5 actions 40-53; T7 action 24; TRACE H action 165
T01 call@288-310; T12 call@1080; T16 expect@50

notes: Kept as inc-010. Combines the region code slices (hint, maxlength, live prefix, empty prefix slot, No clears the code), the origin task's completeness rule, the internal reference hint, the Welsh sweep and the visual baseline: all change the same origin page and its one baseline. Depends on the country search box row (inc-009): the live prefix follows the country picked in that control (DR1 inc-079 tied the live prefix to the country control), and the baseline must show the finished page. If the combiner orders the subdivision label row (req-030) before this one, the baseline also shows it; otherwise that row refreshes the baseline itself.

Completeness: Yes without a code cannot be saved through the page (the page holds the trader with 'Enter the region of origin code'), so the 'Yes needs a code' half of req-034 is guarded by the page's existing validation and the criterion observes the reachable cases; the builder still adds the rule to the origin obligation so a stored Yes with no code is never Complete.

req-057 covers the type and origin pages. The type page lives in the INS front door, so its Welsh is written as a criterion of the type question row (inc-148), which builds in that repo; this row's Welsh criterion covers the origin page strings, and req-057 sits here where the last of them land. The Welsh criterion was narrowed from the earlier 'type and origin pages' because this row does not build in the INS front door.
